references.text: The people of Israel give a similar promise of obedience to Moses at Mount Sinai, where they say they will do all that the Lord has said.
The people answer unanimously that they will do all that the Lord has said, a promise of obedience similar to the one they give to Joshua.
The people confirm their obedience through the covenant and promise to do all that the Lord has commanded.
The people ask Moses to hear God's words and convey them, and they promise to listen and do what is said.
The children of Gad and Reuben promise to do as the Lord has commanded, an expression of obedience to their leader.
The people renew their covenant with Joshua and promise to serve the Lord and listen to his voice.
Samuel warns the people about the consequences of having a king, but they insist on following their decision.
Hebrews encourages believers to obey their leaders, which reflects the people's promise to follow Joshua.
